message.content:
Sure! Just split on the first `"="` only:

```python
temp = "hello=good="
parts = temp.split("=", 1)   # split at most once
print(parts)                # ['hello', 'good=']
```

`split("=", 1)` tells Python to split on `"="` but stop after the first split, so the trailing `"="` stays attached to the second part.

They want code that splits the string `temp` into `["hello", "good="]`. The string is `"hello=good="`. Splitting on "=" would produce `["hello", "good", ""]`. They want to keep the trailing "=" in the second part. So they want to split only on the first "=". In Python, you can use `temp.split("=", 1)` which splits at most once. That would give `["hello", "good="]`. Actually, let's test mentally: `"hello=good=".split("=", 1)` splits at the first "=" only, giving `["hello", "good="]`. Yes.

Alternatively, you could use `temp.partition("=")` which returns a tuple of three parts: before, separator, after. But they specifically want to use `.split()`.

So the answer: `parts = temp.split("=", 1)`.

We can also show printing: `print(parts)`.

Thus the code:

```python
temp = "hello=good="
parts = temp.split("=", 1)
print(parts)  # ['hello', 'good=']
```
